To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a cholinergic differentiating activity was found in extracts of developing and adult sweat glands and that the activity does not appear to be CDF/LIF.

the target gland extracts of the sweat glands contain a cholinergic differentiating factor which is not CDF or LIF and which induces choline acetyl transferase activity and vesoactive intestinal peptide expression while reducing catecholinergic properties and neureopetide Y in cultured sympathetic neurons.
the sympathetic innervation of sweat glands undergoes developmental changes in its neurotransmitter phenotype, which is induced by a target-derived cholinergic differentiation protein.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms that regulate neuronal phenotype in the developing and adult peripheral nervous system.
the mechanisms by which target cells influence the development and maintenance of neuronal phenotypes.
the development of a novel approach to the study of the development of a new class of neurons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the sympathetic innervation of the sweat glands undergoes an age-related change from noradrenergically to cholinergically and peptiderglycally innervated during development, and this change is mediated by a target-derived differentiation factor.
the sweat gland cholinergic differentiation protein is a novel factor that is not identical to any other factor that has been previously described.
the sweat gland cholinergic differentiation factors are different from the CDF/LIF from the heart.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the sweat gland-derived cholinergic differentiation factors (CDF) may be the first identified target-derived factors which are involved in the differentiation of cholinergic neurons in the peripheral nervous system.

we identified a target-derived neuronal CDF in sweat glands that may play a role in the developmental switch of the sympathetic innervation of sweat glands from noradrenergically- to cholinergically- mediated.
the sweat gland extracts contain a heat labile, trypsin sensitive acidic protein that induces cholinergic properties in cultured sympathetic neurons.
The main takeaway from our work is that

sweat glands produce a protein that causes the differentiation of sympathetic neurons into cholinergic neurons, a finding that has implications for understanding the development of sweat glands and the nervous system.
the sweat gland extracts induce cholinergic and peptide expression in cultured sympathetic neurons.
sweat glands are capable of producing a factor that induces cholinergic and vasoactive peptide expression in sympathetic neurons.
